turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, my manager made me come in. I guess... what scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service, or doing things out of order. Like, the other day I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I kept repeating table numbers out loud instead of actually closing out the checks. 

We have a really weird soda machine there, by the way. It’s one of those freestyle ones where you can mix all the flavors? I usually mix cherry and vanilla, but sometimes the syrup gets stuck and it just tastes like carbonated water. Actually, when I was taking classes at the community college a few years ago, I worked at a movie theater that had the exact same machine. I loved that job, but I had to quit because my car broke down and I couldn't afford to fix the alternator. Alternators are so expensive to replace, aren't they? I think it was going to be like five hundred dollars. 

But anyway, yeah, my boss said I was scaring people with the key thing, so here I am.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality and derailment, drifting from the topic of work to a soda machine, a past job, and car repairs before returning to the main point.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes freezing up at work, standing still holding a key, and repetitively saying table numbers out loud, which are disorganized and abnormal behaviors.

turns.doctor_question: Do you remember what happens during those moments when you freeze up, or is it completely blank for you?
turns.patient_response:
I'm not really sure, honestly. It's just... fuzzy, I guess? I don't think it's completely blank, but I can't really tell you what's going through my head either. It's kind of like when you walk into a room and completely forget why you went in there. 

That actually happens to me in the walk-in freezer at work all the time. The door to our freezer is so heavy, and the metal handle gets completely iced over. One time my coworker Jimmy—he's the prep cook, he makes these incredible garlic knots from scratch—he actually got stuck in the walk-in for like twenty minutes because the latch jammed. And he was only wearing his thin little work shirt. They make us wear these black polyester polo shirts that are supposed to be breathable, but they just make you sweat and then you freeze the second you step near the AC vents. 

It's actually really cold in this office, now that I think about it. Do they always keep the air conditioning cranked up this high in here?

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates marked tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from the original topic of their mind going blank to a walk-in freezer, a coworker's experience, work uniforms, and finally the temperature of the doctor's office.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or when nobody was around?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah, actually. Sometimes when I'm closing up the restaurant, or even just when I'm home in my own kitchen, I'll hear a woman's voice. She'll say my name, or she'll tell me I'm doing the till count wrong. It's so clear that I've actually answered out loud before I realize nobody else is there. 

Counting the till is always the worst part of closing anyway. We still use this ancient cash register that jams if you press the buttons too fast. My manager, Greg, refuses to upgrade it because he says it gives the place character. He's always talking about character. He makes us wear these awful suspenders with our uniforms because he thinks it looks authentic. But the clips on them are so cheap, they pop off if you bend down to pick up a napkin. I dropped a whole tray of water glasses once because my suspender snapped and hit me right in the shoulder. Glass went everywhere, all over the dining room floor. The floor is this black and white checkerboard tile, which looks nice, but it shows every single scuff mark and piece of dirt. I spend half my shift just sweeping the same spot by the front door. People track in so much mud, especially when it rains. I actually really like the rain, though. The sound of it hitting the roof is so relaxing. I have a tin roof on my apartment building, and when it storms, it's just the best sound to fall asleep to. 

But yeah, I do hear that voice sometimes. It's just really weird when I answer back and there's nobody around.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly confirms hearing a woman's voice speaking to them when nobody else is present, indicating auditory hallucinations.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from the topic of the voice to cash registers, suspenders, floor tiles, and rain before returning to the original point.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been diagnosed with any physical health problems or medical conditions?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, not really. I've never had any major medical problems or anything like that. I'm pretty healthy. 

I do get a lot of headaches, though, especially when I work the double shifts on the weekends. The fluorescent lights in the kitchen are just so bright, they give me this awful pressure right behind my eyes. I keep telling Greg we should switch to those softer LED bulbs. They're supposed to be way better for your energy bill, too. I read this article online about how much money restaurants waste just on electricity. It's crazy. It's like, no wonder a plate of pasta costs twenty dollars now. Everything is just getting so expensive. I went to buy a carton of eggs the other day and it was almost six dollars. Six dollars! For eggs! I remember when they used to be like, ninety-nine cents. My grandma used to make this amazing egg salad sandwich for me when I was little. She'd put a little bit of paprika in it, which sounds weird, but it was actually so good. She grew her own paprika peppers in her backyard. Her garden was huge, she had tomatoes and cucumbers and these giant sunflowers that were taller than I was. I always wanted to plant sunflowers on my balcony, but it doesn't get enough sunlight because of the big oak tree across the street. The squirrels in that tree are so aggressive, they literally throw acorns at my cat when he sits in the window. 

But anyway, no, no big physical health problems or diagnoses or anything. Just the headaches from the lights.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates clear tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from headaches to lightbulbs, energy bills, inflation, eggs, their grandmother's garden, and finally to squirrels.

turns.doctor_question: About how long has it been since you first started hearing that woman's voice?
turns.patient_response:
Um, well, the really clear ones, like that woman's voice when I'm closing? And also, I've been having these really strong feelings that some of my coworkers and even the customers are kind of... targeting me, or watching me? That's all been going on for about four months now. 

It started right around the time Greg hired this new guy, Jason, to work the fry station. Jason is always whispering to the other line cooks when I walk by to pick up an order. He wears these really loud, colorful bandanas on his head instead of a normal hairnet. I don't even know if that's up to health code. The health inspector came in last month and docked us points because the walk-in fridge was two degrees too warm. Greg threw an absolute fit about it. He made us all stay an hour late to scrub the grout in the prep area. Scrubbing grout is the worst, you have to use a toothbrush to really get in there. I have this electric toothbrush at home that my dentist recommended, an Oral-B one. It has a little timer that buzzes every thirty seconds so you know to switch to a different part of your mouth. Dental care is so important, you know? If you don't take care of your teeth, it can lead to heart disease. I saw a documentary about that on Netflix once. Netflix has so many documentaries now, it's hard to find an actual movie to watch. I just want to watch a good romantic comedy sometimes, like the ones from the nineties with Meg Ryan. She always had the best hair in those movies. 

But yeah, it's been about four months since the voices got really clear and I started noticing people acting strange around me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a strong belief that coworkers and customers are targeting or watching them, indicating persecutory delusions.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient confirms hearing a woman's voice, which is an auditory hallucination.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and loose associations, drifting from the topic of a coworker to health codes, toothbrushes, Netflix, and Meg Ryan movies.
